challenge.method: Test three possible errors separately: a reference to a different publisher tool, release attribution based solely on a version label, and inferred generation based solely on matching fields. Compare the publisher paths, the two pinned records, both annotated tag targets, the full generated commit and the time-ordered job lines.
challenge.results: The publisher's zero/1.0 edition and the SPDX legalcode suffix identify the CC0 instrument. The XML and data v3.29.0 tags directly target their respective file pins. The job fetches the full XML target, records the build with the generated commit prefix and matching message, and pushes from the prefix of that commit's recorded parent to the prefix of the commit itself. Together these observations support causal release lineage for the inspected JSON.

limitations: The crosswalk documents an SPDX entry and its reference. It establishes neither text equivalence nor copyright classification, project-specific grants or adoption of CC0 by any project.

The XML, generated data, corresponding tags, build commit and job records share SPDX information lineage. Release and build records establish provenance within that lineage. Both annotated tags and the build commit are reported unsigned.
The three job lines document a fetch, commit and push. They do not show every intervening command, the complete build environment or a bit-for-bit reproduction.
reasoning: The generated JSON identifies CC0-1.0 as “Creative Commons Zero v1.0 Universal”, marks the identifier as nondeprecated and points to https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode. The source XML at its separate pin gives the same ID, name and legal-code URL. Creative Commons' own title, canonical edition path and operative plaintext establish which publisher instrument the reference identifies. The annotated tags establish release membership. The job and commit records additionally connect the fetched XML revision to generation and publication of the data revision containing this file.
